newsitem.title: USA: Treasury's Summers defends Clinton education plan.
newsitem.headline: Treasury's Summers defends Clinton education plan.

text.p: Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers on Wednesday defended the administration's plan to provide tax incentives for higher education and denied that they would lead to inflation in tuition.

In testimony prepared for delivery to the Senate Finance Committee, Summers argued that colleges and universities would find it difficult to raise tuition because of what he called "significant competition" for first-year students.
The administration's plan includes tax credits and deductions designed to make college more affordable for lower and middle income families.
Some critics have charged that the plan will merely lead to higher tuition charges and not actually benefit students.
